reason:
Compared the complete original def:regular at source lines 374-385, the determinant and edge-tail conventions, and def:polygon's explicit labelled/equivariant formalization permission with SM.regular_definition and all concrete definitions and proof dependencies supplying its meaning. The aggregate assumes only the inherited n>=3 and an arbitrary real planar labelled tuple P. Its local principal-turn clause is quantified at every index with exactly the printed local two-edge domain. It does not require the whole polygon to be regular or generic merely to define or characterize a locally valid principal turn.

Plane is the previously verified actual pair of real coordinates. planeDot is precisely u1*v1+u2*v2. euclideanLength uses the norm of the coordinate complex number, and euclideanLength_formula proves it equals sqrt(u1*u1+u2*u2); the product-space maximum norm is not being used in the source cosine denominator. cornerRotor is conjugate(planeComplex incoming) times planeComplex outgoing. Its proved real part is the actual dot product, its imaginary part is the source positive determinant det(incoming,outgoing), and its norm is the product of the two Euclidean lengths. Thus both the angle orientation and normalization agree with the source, including the source's incoming edge at i-1 and outgoing edge at i. These are coordinate identities, not supplied geometric-orientation assumptions.

RegularPair requires both vectors nonzero and excludes exactly the existence of a strictly negative real multiplier carrying the incoming vector to the outgoing vector. It does not impose a nonzero determinant or exclude positive collinearity. scalar_of_det_zero derives the actual scalar from dot(u,v)/dot(u,u), with denominator positivity proved from nonzero u. The negative/positive multiplier equivalences with signed dot product and zero determinant are consequently proved from the coordinates. The negative-real-axis exclusion for the complex rotor is proved equivalent to the intended non-antiparallel condition on nonzero vectors; no stronger slit-plane premise is exposed in the source aggregate.

principalAngle is the actual complex argument of that rotor. I inspected the pinned Mathlib definition and the used Arg lemmas: the general argument lies in (-pi,pi], its cosine is real-part/norm for a nonzero rotor, its negative sign is characterized by negative imaginary part, and the value pi occurs precisely on the negative real axis. The proof removes pi using the proved regular domain and retains the strict lower bound. PrincipalAngleSpec is exactly the source's strict interval (-pi,pi), the Euclidean normalized cosine equality, and equality of the signs of angle and determinant. It contains no nonzero-vector, regularity, desired-existence, uniqueness or supplied-angle premise. principalAngle_spec proves the actual constructed angle satisfies those three printed conditions. The sign proof covers negative, zero and positive cases; in the zero-determinant case regularity rules out the antiparallel alternative.

Uniqueness is independently proved for arbitrary angles satisfying only that exact specification. Cosine equality gives equality of their absolute values because both absolute values lie in [0,pi), where cosine is injective; the common sign then reconstructs the signed angle. Conversely, any solution of PrincipalAngleSpec forces both vectors nonzero: a zero vector forces angle zero by the sign equation but makes the normalized dot product zero, contradicting cos(0)=1. A negative scalar multiple similarly forces angle zero while its normalized dot product is negative, again a contradiction. Thus existence implies the actual regular-pair predicate; it is not assumed or built into the specification. principalAngle_existsUnique_iff proves the converse through the explicit argument construction. Although principalAngle is implemented as a total real-valued function, the source existence assertion is existence of a solution to PrincipalAngleSpec, not merely existence of that total function value. Excluded degenerate pairs therefore have no accidentally certified principal turn. The use of unique existence in the locus equivalence agrees with the source existence wording because specification uniqueness is proved without a regularity premise.

Regular is the all-indices actual regular-pair predicate. regular_iff_edges proves equivalence to exactly all outgoing edges nonzero and no outgoing edge a negative multiple of its incoming edge; the incoming nonzero condition is obtained from the preceding index, rather than added as a stronger global condition. regular_iff_principalTurns_exist proves the complete all-principal-turns characterization. Generic inclusion is a theorem derived from the previously accepted G1 nonzero-edge and no-real-multiple conclusions; Generic is not part of the regular locus's definition or the general local-angle domain. principalTurn_eq_zero_iff proves, on precisely the printed local domain, that zero principal turn is equivalent to an actual strictly positive real multiple. Positive collinear consecutive edges are thus included and receive the source zero angle.

Finally, regular_shift proves the locus invariant under every cyclic shift, and principalTurn_shift proves the exact index-equivariance formula: the principal turn at new i for shift a P equals the old principal turn at i+a. The source introduces all constructions on representatives up to induced relabelling and explicitly permits labelled tuples throughout with proved equivariance. These full laws supply that authorized polygon reading without a distinguished label or an additional quotient assumption. No assertion about reversal, rotation-number integrality, path constancy, subdivision, or wall/soft laws is smuggled into this definition review.

The source hash, all 10 inspected local supporting-file hashes, and the independently recomputed semantic dependency hash match the passed checkpoint-019 development receipt. The five new modules are unchanged from this independent source/type/body review; the five inherited geometric modules are byte-identical to earlier independent reviews. The receipt audits 644 project declarations and 17 mapped claims, with only the standard propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound axioms, and explicitly leaves stage_accepted false. This review certifies only the complete original DEFINE row def:regular. It does not certify the still-unproved full lem:rot, the corner state sum, or the main wall-crossing/soft-theorem targets. Supporting Euclidean, scalar, argument and uniqueness lemmas are not counted as additional original claims.

countersignature_20260913.reason: Source def:regular (reference/SM/sm-1-polygons.tex:386-396; SM15 excerpt byte-identical to SM12, sm15_reworded=false) has four contents: (1) for an index i with l_{i-1}, l_i != 0 and l_i not a negative real multiple of l_{i-1}, the principal turn theta_i in (-pi,pi) is the unique angle with cos theta_i = <l_{i-1},l_i>/(|l_{i-1}||l_i|) and sgn theta_i = sgn det(l_{i-1},l_i); (2) R_n = polygons with all l_i != 0 and no l_i a negative multiple of l_{i-1}, equivalently all principal turns exist; (3) every generic polygon lies in R_n; (4) theta_i = 0 iff l_i is a positive multiple of l_{i-1}. Lean (work/lean/SM/RegularDefinition.lean:13-24, hypotheses only 3 <= n and an arbitrary P : ZMod n -> R x R, matching def:polygon's n >= 3 and the sanctioned labelled-tuple reading at sm-1-polygons.tex:56-62): RegularPair u v := u != 0 /\ v != 0 /\ not exists r < 0, v = r . u (RegularPairs.lean:8-9) applied to u = edge P (i-1), v = edge P i with edge P i = P(i+1) - P i (Polygon.lean:49), exactly the printed two-edge domain with the printed tail convention. PrincipalAngleSpec u v theta := -pi < theta < pi /\ cos theta = planeDot u v / (euclideanLength u * euclideanLength v) /\ sign theta = sign (det u v) (PrincipalAngles.lean:9-12), where planeDot = u1 v1 + u2 v2, euclideanLength = complex norm of (u1,u2) i.e. Euclidean length, det = u1 v2 - u2 v1 (Polygon.lean:16) matching the convention at sm-1-polygons.tex:5; so the spec is the printed characterization verbatim. principalTurn P i := arg(conj(l_{i-1}) * l_i) (RegularLocus.lean:15-16, EuclideanPlane.lean cornerRotor, RegularPairs.lean principalAngle), and clause 4 of the theorem asserts, on exactly the printed local domain, that this value satisfies the spec, is the unique such value, and vanishes iff exists r > 0 with l_i = r . l_{i-1} -- contents (1) and (4). Regular P := forall i, RegularPair (edge P (i-1)) (edge P i) (RegularLocus.lean:12-13); theorem clauses 1-2 give Regular <-> (forall i, edge P i != 0 /\ no negative multiple) and Regular <-> (forall i, exists! theta, Spec) -- content (2) with both printed characterizations (exists! is the right reading of 'the unique angle'). Clause 3, Generic P -> Regular P with Generic := G1 /\ G2 (Generic.lean:11-19, matching def:generic at sm-1-polygons.tex:100-108), is content (3). Clauses 5-6 record shift-invariance of Regular and the index-equivariance principalTurn (shift a P) i = principalTurn P (i+a), which is what the formalization remark requires for the labelled definitions to denote notions on polygons. Nothing is vacuous: n >= 3 makes ZMod n = Fin n, the domains are satisfiable, and the definitions carry no hidden genericity or nonzero-determinant premise (positive collinear consecutive edges are correctly kept in the regular domain and get turn 0). Existing review work/reviews/def-regular.json reaches the same verdict; its recorded file hashes match the current files.
stronger_than_source: Clauses 5-6 (RegularDefinition.lean:22-23): Regular (shift a P) <-> Regular P and principalTurn (shift a P) i = principalTurn P (i + a) are not printed in def:regular; they are the shift-equivariance that the formalization remark (sm-1-polygons.tex:56-62) asks a labelled-tuple formalization to record, so they justify rather than exceed the printed 'polygon' reading.

principalTurn is a total real-valued function (junk value = Complex.arg of the rotor off the domain) whereas the source only defines theta_i on the two-edge domain; the theorem asserts its properties only under RegularPair, so no off-domain claim is made about the printed object.
